notes.decision: Translated as 'strike (them) / strike upon' throughout. The recurring verb ⲟⲁⲡ (lines 3, 6, 30) and reduplicated ⲟⲁⲙⲟⲙ (line 4) function in parallel with attested ⲧⲱⲙⲧ ⲁⲣⲁϩ 'reach upon' (line 8) and ⲧⲉⲍⲁϩ 'reach' (line 27, 29) as verbs of archonic violent contact with their targets. Etymology uncertain — possibly Lyc reflex of a striking-verb (cf. ⲱⲡ 'count, render judgment upon' under semantic shift). The two forms (ⲟⲁⲡ vs reduplicated ⲟⲁⲙⲟⲙ) may be morphological variants of the same root.

Parsed as habitual negative ⲙⲁⲩ-ⲣ̄-ⲁⲅⲁⲑⲟⲛ 'they do no good' (Greek ἀγαθόν, with regular Lyc. ⲫ for ⲑ) + ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ 'ever' (Lyc for ⲉⲛⲉϩ). Translation: 'they never do any good' = 'they are utterly unprofitable.' This explains why the angels strike them: the cloud-archons are inveterately destructive.

ⲣ̄ⲫⲟⲣⲉ from Greek φορεῖν 'wear (as garment)' (cf. accumulated vocabulary). With locative ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϩ/ⲙⲙⲁⲩ 'there' the construction means 'don themselves (in disguise) there.' The cloud-archons clothe themselves in a robber-disguise upon arriving at their target locale — matching the ⲗⲏⲥⲧⲏⲥ 'thief/robber' simile that follows.

Parsed as ⲡⲉⲧ- (relative) + ⲁⲩ-ⲟⲩⲱⲛ-ⲙⲁⲓ̈ⲧ-ⲁⲣⲁϩ '[which] they have opened the way upon (it).' The tree is one along their destructive route. Alternative parsing as 'on which they have set the path' yields the same sense. Confidence moderate due to lacuna and unusual idiom.

ⲭⲉⲥⲧ 'convey upward' (per accumulated vocabulary, normally salvific) here used cosmologically of the cloud being lifted up against the Virgin of Light — a hostile ascent (cf. accumulated entry ⲭⲉⲥⲧ ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ ⲟⲩⲃⲉ 'rise up against'). The 3sg.f object suffix -ⲥ refers to ⲧⲕⲗⲟⲟⲗⲉ 'the cloud.'

Translated as 'the place' (Lyc. variant of ⲡⲙⲁ). Could alternatively read as 'the water' (Lyc. for ⲡⲙⲟⲟⲩ) which would fit the cloud-formation context naturally. Both readings yield coherent sense; 'the place' (the lower world from which the cloud rises) preferred for parallel with ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ 'the upper place.'

Translated as 'the form/likeness.' Likely Lyc. compound ⲥⲙ-ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'form-likeness' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲓⲥⲛⲩ 'this manner/fashion' on ⲥⲙⲟⲧ + ⲉⲓⲛⲉ). Functions as identifying noun: 'the form is that of the thunders and lightnings.'
Translated as 'the lightnings.' Paired with ⲛⲓⲍⲣⲟⲩⲙⲡⲉ 'the thunders' (in glossary). Likely a Lycopolitan term for lightning — cf. tentative ⲙⲉⲕⲡⲉ 'lightning' in glossary. Etymology uncertain.

Two distinct cold-weather terms in the trio with ⲭⲁⲗⲁⲍⲁ 'hail' (Greek χάλαζα). ⲭⲓⲱⲛ = Greek χιών 'snow.' ⲭⲉϩ likely native Coptic ϫⲁϥ 'frost' or analogous term. Translated as 'frost / hail / snow' to preserve the threefold inventory of destructive precipitation.

Translated 'while my members' literally. The first-person possessive 'my' is striking — likely the perspective shifts here to the cosmic Living Soul / Cross of Light speaking, whose 'members' (= the light-particles dispersed through creation) are the targets struck by the archons. This shift commonly occurs in Manichaean cosmological discourse where the suffering Cross of Light speaks in first person.
